correctness.rationale: For Z=X⊕pℓ1(Γ) and point z=(x,v), a norming dual functional has radial Hölder components r,s with r^p+s^p=1. In every slice, a Daugavet-far X coordinate and a nearly norming atomic coordinate produce distance ≥[(A+r)^p+(B-M+|s-M|)^p]^(1/p). The one-atom discrepancy B-c+|s-c| decreases in c, hence its minimum at the maximum atom M. Conversely, increasingly thin slices at a maximal atom force the pair of summand norms toward (r,s) by strict Hölder equality and force the ℓ1 vector toward s·sgn(vγ)eγ; this gives the matching upper bound. Covers uncountable Γ since v has countable support and nonzero maximum attained. Independently minimized the p=2 pure-atomic function F(s)=1-s²+(1-M+|s-M|)² for M=.2,.5,.8; it yields 2(1-M) when M≤1/2 and 4(1-M)² when M≥1/2. Finite rational verifier is a diagnostic, not an infinite proof. Requires nontrivial Daugavet Banach component for X* norming slices; no general formula asserted for arbitrary X.
